S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

info.persona: An energetic yet slightly disorganized 52‑year‑old construction professional, Han Yuen blends hands‑on curiosity with a green‑retrofit vision, juggling tool‑obsessed hobbies, garden‑grown meals, and a constant undercurrent of stress‑driven worry.
info.professional_persona: Han Yuen, a 52‑year‑old construction veteran in San Francisco, blends three decades of hands‑on expertise in concrete formwork, timber framing, and heavy‑equipment operation with a curious eye for sustainable retrofits, using their practical problem‑solving and assertive crew leadership to bridge on‑site challenges with emerging green building methods while often juggling last‑minute schedule tweaks due to a relaxed approach to planning.
info.cultural_background: Han was born to immigrant parents from Taiwan who settled in San Francisco's Richmond District. Growing up, his household blended traditional Taiwanese customs—such as celebrating Lunar New Year, preparing xiaolongbao, and honoring ancestors—with the multicultural vibe of the Bay Area. Bilingual in Mandarin and English, he often helped translate for older neighbors and participated in community events at the local Buddhist temple. The values of hard work, respect for elders, and collective responsibility instilled by his family continue to influence his approach to teamwork and mentorship on construction sites. While his divorce has shifted some personal dynamics, he maintains close ties with his extended family and frequently joins them for holiday gatherings and cultural festivals.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Han enjoys hands‑on hobbies that let him unwind while still satisfying his curiosity. He tends a modest rooftop garden where he grows herbs and leafy greens, a practice that blends his love of nature with practical food production. He is an avid photographer, capturing the changing skyline of San Francisco and the intricate details of construction sites. On quieter days, he works on DIY home improvement projects, from building a custom coffee table to repairing old plumbing. He frequents local parks for brisk walks or jogs, using the time to clear his mind and manage stress. He also participates in community board‑game nights and occasionally volunteers at a neighborhood garden, which satisfies his cooperative side while providing a social outlet.
info.sports_persona: Han Yuen stays fit by jogging along the Embarcadero and joining the Bay Area Runners club for weekend miles, cheerfully rooting for the San Francisco Giants in baseball and the Golden State Warriors in basketball, and occasionally joining a pickup basketball game at the local community center, balancing a love of outdoor activity with a low‑key approach to structured training.
info.arts_persona: Han Yuen channels their creative side through street photography of the ever‑changing San Francisco skyline, drawing inspiration from Michael Kenna, while spending board‑game nights with friends and attending occasional jazz sessions at The Fillmore featuring artists like Kamasi Washington, reflecting a blend of visual precision and auditory appreciation.
info.travel_persona: Han Yuen prefers low‑key weekend getaways to nearby Napa vineyards or the misty coast of Mendocino, planning trips on a whim with a backpack of garden tools for inspiration, yet they dream of a future pilgrimage to Copenhagen to study Danish sustainable architecture and to Kyoto for its historic temples, balancing a modest travel budget with a yearning for cultural immersion.
info.culinary_persona: Han Yuen enjoys cooking with fresh basil, cilantro, and mint from their rooftop garden, whipping up homemade pesto, spicy stir‑fry, and hearty sourdough‑based clam chowder, while also savoring a perfectly pulled espresso at a local café, showcasing a competent but not gourmet‑level culinary skill set that leans toward practical, herb‑forward meals.

info.persona: Joann Watkins blends meticulous bookkeeping expertise with community‑centered creativity, garden‑fresh culinary experiments, and a habit of over‑scheduling volunteer commitments, all while they navigate occasional anxiety through daily mindfulness journaling.
info.professional_persona: Joann Watkins, a meticulous bookkeeping consultant on the cusp of retirement, applies their decades of experience with QuickBooks, Sage, and advanced Excel macros to streamline finances for local small businesses, while they mentor newer staff with an organized, approachable, yet occasionally assertive style that reflects their balanced curiosity and practicality.
info.cultural_background: Joann grew up in the rural suburbs of upstate New York, descended from a lineage of German and Irish settlers who arrived in the region in the late 19th century. The close‑knit agricultural community of Morrisonville shaped her values of hard work, self‑reliance, and mutual support. She has been an active member of the town’s Episcopal church for decades, participating in community outreach and seasonal festivals such as the Clinton County Fair. While her cultural roots are grounded in traditional American small‑town customs—family gatherings, church potlucks, and local volunteering—Joann also embraces a broader curiosity about the world, evident in her ongoing genealogy pursuits and willingness to adopt new technologies in her profession.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Joann is an active participant in community life. She spends many mornings tending to a vegetable garden and a flower bed that she shares with neighbors, finding the routine both grounding and rewarding. She is a regular at the local bridge club and enjoys the strategic challenge of card games. Her sociable streak shines through in her volunteer work with the town theater, where she assists with set design and costume organization. Joann loves walking the nearby trails of the Plattsburgh‑Ausable Preserve, often combining the outings with bird‑watching. She is an avid reader of cozy mystery novels and a passionate experimenter in the kitchen, frequently hosting dinner parties to showcase new recipes. Her creative side surfaces in quilting and needlework, and she participates in the church choir. To satisfy her curiosity, Joann researches her family genealogy, and she maintains a daily journaling practice that includes mindfulness exercises to help manage her occasional anxiety.
info.sports_persona: Joann Watkins, an avid walker and bird‑watcher, spends mornings on the Plattsburgh‑Ausable Preserve trails and participates in the local senior walking club, while they root for the New York Rangers, Buffalo Bills, and Adirondack Thunder, and they treat each weekend hike as a low‑impact fitness routine.
info.arts_persona: Joann Watkins, a devoted community theater volunteer, quilter, and choir singer, crafts intricate patchwork quilts inspired by Faith Ringgold, enjoys the gospel harmonies of Mahalia Jackson, immerses themselves in Agatha Christie mysteries, and they find artistic fulfillment in the lively productions of the Plattsburgh Community Theater.
info.travel_persona: Joann Watkins, a nostalgic road‑tripper, has explored historic New England towns like Burlington and Stowe, trekked the Alexander Hamilton Trail in Canada, while they dream of touring the English Lake District to trace the origins of beloved cozy mystery settings, and they prefer modest, well‑planned itineraries that respect their fixed retirement budget and family responsibilities.
info.culinary_persona: Joann Watkins, a passionate home chef, frequently prepares herb‑roasted chicken seasoned with garden‑fresh rosemary and thyme, simmered vegetable stew featuring heirloom tomatoes, and a seasonal apple‑crumble dessert, while they showcase their intermediate cooking skills by hosting themed dinner parties that delight friends and neighbors.

info.persona: Diego Camacho is a gregarious CNC whiz who talks faster than a milling spindle, habitually stays up late tweaking Arduino bots, yet forgets to water houseplants, and they balance a restless curiosity with a genuine love for community.
info.professional_persona: Diego Camacho, a 20‑year‑old CNC enthusiast, blends a hands‑on mastery of Haas and Fanuc controllers with a curious knack for Python‑driven workflow tweaks, while their talkative, team‑oriented nature makes them the go‑to mentor on the shop floor for new operators.
info.cultural_background: Diego grew up in a Mexican‑American household in Washington State, where Spanish was spoken at home and Mexican traditions were celebrated alongside local customs. His family emphasizes respect, cooperation, and community harmony, values that shape his considerate and cooperative nature. He participates in cultural events such as Día de los Muertos and Mexican Independence Day festivals, and he regularly prepares classic dishes like tamales and pozole for friends. Bilingual and bicultural, Diego often serves as a bridge between his Mexican heritage and his Pacific‑Northwest environment, bringing a warm, sociable presence to both his workplace and community activities.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When he’s not on the shop floor, Diego enjoys playing soccer in a community league, cooking and sharing traditional Mexican dishes with friends and family, and jamming on his acoustic guitar. He frequently tinkers with Arduino‑based robotics projects and 3D‑prints custom parts, which satisfies his curiosity for new tools. Outdoor activities like hiking in the Columbia River Gorge and photographing the Pacific Northwest landscape provide a balance to his technical work. He is also an active participant in online multiplayer games and volunteers at a bilingual STEM outreach program for middle‑school students.
info.sports_persona: Diego Camacho, a 20‑year‑old soccer enthusiast, dribbles for the Columbia River Community Soccer League on weekends, cheers for the Seattle Sounders FC during the MLS season, keeps fit with early‑morning hikes in the Columbia River Gorge, and they occasionally join pick‑up basketball games at the local rec center.
info.arts_persona: Diego Camacho strums acoustic renditions of José González and Rodrigo y Gabriela while riffing with friends, curates a modest vinyl collection that includes The Strokes and classic mariachi recordings, captures mist‑shrouded Pacific Northwest vistas in the style of Ansel Adams, and they often share the photos on a photography Discord server.
info.travel_persona: Diego Camacho plans weekend road trips to Oregon’s Columbia River Gorge, savors occasional camping trips to Mt. Rainier, and dreams of backpacking through the Andes of Peru and the historic sites of Spain's Andalusia, balancing their modest student budget with a love for low‑cost hostels and shared rides, and they keep a travel journal filled with sketches of each destination.
info.culinary_persona: Diego Camacho cooks with a flair for masa‑based dishes like tamales and chilaquiles, layers flavors with chipotle, cilantro, and fresh lime, experiments with 3D‑printed spice racks, and they treat friends to homemade horchata and queso fundido after a long shop shift.
